title: In home recordings, 10-month babble matched consonants in caregivers' speech
summary: Laing and Bergelson found that 44 infants at 10 to 11 months babbled consonants that matched the consonants in their caregivers' speech.
body: Catherine Laing and Elika Bergelson analyzed naturalistic home recordings of 44 infants aged 10 to 11 months. They report that the infants' babble matched the consonants in their caregivers' speech. Infants who already had a well-established set of consonants also matched their babble to objects in the environment. The paper's claim is about that sample of recordings. It does not say babble has no pattern, and it does not say every infant at 10 months matches objects.

sources.title: From babble to words: Infants' early productions match words and objects in their environment
sources.author: Catherine Laing and Elika Bergelson
sources.note: Opened 2026-11-26 at the PMC page. Supports the abstract: 44 infants aged 10 to 11 months, babble matching caregiver consonants, and object matching when the consonant repertoire is well established.
